blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) has urged Filipinos to take precautions, warning that strong movement along the Manila Trench could generate a tsunami reaching 5.5 meters. On Tuesday, Phivolcs outlined its tsunami risk reduction initiatives ahead of World Tsunami Awareness Day on November 5. During a press conference, Director Mylene Villegas was asked whether the Manila Trench or the West Valley Fault could trigger a strong tsunami. Villegas explained that movement along the Manila Trench could generate a tsunami, while movement along the West Valley Fault could cause earthquakes on land, particularly the “Big One.” […]...
